title: Shiftory agent-quality lost/unrecoverable generation attempt
description: A record of a generation attempt whose raw output bytes were never recoverable at all -- distinct from invalidated-capture-v1, which archives an ACTUAL, hash-verified raw response that was later withdrawn. This schema exists specifically for the registry_version 2 shared-prompt-directory defect: two invocations (config-a and config-b of the same case) were pointed at one shared directory, both wrote RAW_RESPONSE to the same path, and one silently overwrote the other before either byte stream was ever read by agent_harness.capture_result -- so there is no raw response, no sha256, and no explanation to preserve for the overwritten invocation. This record exists so the incident is honestly represented as structured, machine-readable data (never merely prose disclosure), while being explicit that it cannot be audited the way a real capture archive can: there are no bytes to hash-verify. Fields that were never genuinely observed are null with an explicit reason, never fabricated.

orchestrator_agent_handle.description: The caller-supplied name given to the orchestrating session's own sub-agent-launch tool for this specific invocation -- recoverable from the orchestrator's own still-idle agent registry after the incident, and thus real, though (like agent-run-v2's orchestrator_agent_handle) never provider- or platform-issued attestation.

protocol_commit.description: The benchmark_protocol_commit this invocation was generated under -- the commit that was current when the invocation was launched, not the later commit that superseded it.

provenance_limitation.description: An explicit statement of exactly what is, and is not, known about this attempt -- never implying the raw bytes were inspected, scored, or ruled out as a cherry-pick candidate.

orchestrator_reported_metadata.description: Whatever the orchestrator's own tooling reports about this invocation after the fact (elapsed time since launch, turn count) -- explicitly labeled as orchestrator-tool-reported bookkeeping, never provider-confirmed generation timing or duration.
